page: Amazon Web Services c4.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor. This x86_64 architecture server features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs, consisting of 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.9 GHz. It is equipped with 30.0 GB of system memory, providing 1.88 GB of RAM per core, and operates on the Xen hypervisor. The CPU includes 25 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instruction sets. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate average performance across standard compute workloads. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1182.0 and a multi-core score of 7354.0, alongside a Passmark CPU score of 15674.33. In memory bandwidth tests, it reached 851.49 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 89.52 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrated a static web serving throughput of 11.52 GB/sec and processed 6.16 million Redis SET operations per second. Small-model LLM inference reached 163.35 tokens/sec for text generation, though performance drops significantly on larger models, with 7B model prompt processing registering at 23.37 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4.4xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory profile tailored for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints or local NVMe storage. The lack of local storage means storage configurations are decoupled from the compute instance. This instance is suited for workloads such as software compilation, where it achieved a Geekbench clang compilation score of 13105.0, as well as web serving, multi-threaded decompression, and moderate database operations.
